- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

1	# Contributing
2	
3	BoringStack is a monorepo. Each app has its own contributor guide with the
4	patterns and lint rules specific to that surface:
5	
6	- [apps/api/CONTRIBUTING.md](apps/api/CONTRIBUTING.md) — Elysia routes,
7	  Drizzle schemas, audit log requirements, the `bun run check` contract.
8	- [apps/ui/CONTRIBUTING.md](apps/ui/CONTRIBUTING.md) — feature folders,
9	  TanStack Query patterns, i18n, RTL tests.
10	- [apps/docs/DEPLOY.md](apps/docs/DEPLOY.md) — how the
11	  [boringstack.xyz](https://boringstack.xyz) docs site is wired up on
12	  Cloudflare Pages (build settings, custom domain, rollback flow).
13	
14	This document covers what's true for any change anywhere in the repo.
15	
16	## Local setup
17	
18	From a fresh fork:
19	
20	```sh
21	./setup.sh --up
22	```
23	
24	That copies `.env`, generates the GlitchTip secret, and brings the full
25	Compose stack up: Postgres, Valkey, api-dev with migrations applied,
26	ui-dev on `localhost:7331`, OpenAPI client generated. No local Bun or
27	Postgres needed.
28	
29	Create an account at `http://localhost:7331` — signup is open in dev and
30	the verification email lands in the local Mailpit (or use the seeded demo
31	account: uncomment `SUPERUSER_EMAIL` / `SUPERUSER_PASSWORD` in
32	`infra/compose/compose/.env` **before** first boot and the migrator seeds
33	it for you).
34	
35	## The merge bar
36	
37	Every PR runs `bun run validate` in each touched app. CI runs the same
38	script. Local green is CI green.
39	
40	`validate` chains:
41	
42	1. typecheck (`tsc --noEmit`)
43	2. lint (`eslint --max-warnings 0`)
44	3. unit + integration tests
45	4. build
46	
47	Plus the cross-cutting workflows:
48	
49	- `openapi-drift` — fails the PR if `apps/ui/src/lib/api/schema.d.ts` is
50	  stale against the live API contract. Regenerate with
51	  `cd apps/ui && OPENAPI_URL=http://localhost:7330/swagger/json bun run generate:api`.
52	- `full-stack-smoke` — boots the compose stack and runs the Playwright
53	  e2e suite against a freshly migrated DB.
54	
55	## Commits
56	
57	- Signed commits required on `main`. Set up signing before pushing.
58	- Squash-merges only. Commit messages on PRs become the squashed commit
59	  message — write them so they read well in `git log`.
60	- Conventional prefixes (`feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `chore:`,
61	  `docs:`) are honored by the changelog generator.
62	
63	## Lint rules
64	
65	The lint config is strict on purpose:
66	
67	- No `any` (use `unknown` + narrow)
68	- No `as` casting (only `as const`)
69	- No non-null `!`
70	- No floating promises
71	- No `eslint-disable` inline — if a rule fights real intent, edit
72	  `eslint.config.js` and explain why in the PR
73	
74	Architectural plugins enforce import boundaries, audit-log coverage on
75	mutating service methods, transactional multi-write paths, sibling tests
76	for every `*.service.ts` / `*.routes.ts` / `*.utils.ts`, and account
77	scoping on every query that touches an account-scoped table.
78	
79	## Reporting bugs
80	
81	Open an issue at
82	[github.com/boringstack-xyz/boringstack/issues](https://github.com/boringstack-xyz/boringstack/issues).
83	Security issues go through the [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) flow, not the
84	public tracker.

1	# Copy to compose/.env (see .gitignore). Used by compose/dev.sh.
2	#
3	# Dev DX: browser hits Vite at http://localhost:7331 and Vite's dev-server
4	# proxy forwards /api/* to the api-dev container over the docker network.
5	# Same-origin from the browser's perspective — no CORS preflights, no
6	# `.localhost` subdomains, no Traefik in dev.
7	#
8	# Prod routing: Traefik on the apex domain path-routes /api/* + /health to
9	# the api container, everything else to the ui container. One TLS cert,
10	# one host, same-origin everywhere.
11	
12	# dev | prod (which Compose overlay to merge)
13	STACK=dev
14	
15	# Postgres / Valkey (base stack)
16	POSTGRES_USER=app
17	POSTGRES_PASSWORD=app_dev_password
18	POSTGRES_DB=app
19	
20	# Production overlay only: real DNS name for ACME + Traefik router.
21	# The SPA is built domain-agnostic (VITE_API_URL=""), so this single host
22	# serves both the UI and /api/* in same-origin mode.
23	PUBLIC_UI_HOST=example.com
24	ACME_EMAIL=you@example.com
25	
26	# Required in prod (STACK=prod). Compose fails boot with a clear error if
27	# any are unset. Generate JWT_SECRET with `openssl rand -base64 48`.
28	# Generate MFA_ENCRYPTION_KEY with `openssl rand -base64 32`.
29	# JWT_SECRET=
30	# MFA_ENCRYPTION_KEY=
31	# FRONTEND_URL=https://example.com
32	# PUBLIC_API_URL=https://example.com         # origin only — the SPA appends /api/v1 itself
33	# ALLOWED_ORIGINS=   # leave empty for same-origin; set if exposing api cross-origin
34	
35	# GHCR image source. Defaults point at the canonical upstream images. If you
36	# clicked "Use this template" on GitHub, set these to your fork:
37	#
38	#   IMAGE_OWNER       — your GitHub org or user (lowercase). Always set after fork.
39	#   API_IMAGE_NAME    — API image package (default: boringstack-api).
40	#   UI_IMAGE_NAME     — UI image package  (default: boringstack-ui).
41	#   API_IMAGE_TAG     — REQUIRED in prod: semver (v0.1.0) or sha-<digest>.
42	#                       `latest` is rejected (dev.sh fails closed) — prod
43	#                       deploys must be reproducible and auditable.
44	#   UI_IMAGE_TAG      — same.
45	#
46	# IMAGE_OWNER=boringstack-xyz
47	# API_IMAGE_NAME=boringstack-api
48	# UI_IMAGE_NAME=boringstack-ui
49	# API_IMAGE_TAG=v0.1.0
50	# UI_IMAGE_TAG=v0.1.0
51	#
52	# Alternatively, override the full image reference (skips the assembly above):
53	# API_IMAGE=ghcr.io/me/my-saas-api:0.3.0
54	# UI_IMAGE=ghcr.io/me/my-saas-ui:0.5.1
55	
56	# Optional: explicit origin baked into the SPA prod build. Leave unset for
57	# same-origin (the SPA uses relative `/api/*`). Override only if you deploy
58	# the API on a different host (cross-origin) and also set ALLOWED_ORIGINS
59	# in api.prod.env. ORIGIN ONLY — no path suffix. The SPA appends `/api/v1`
60	# itself, so `https://example.com/api` would produce `/api/api/v1/...`.
61	# PUBLIC_API_URL=https://api.example.com
62	
63	# --- Observability (Grafana + Prometheus + Loki + Tempo) ----------------
64	# On by default for dev + prod (`./dev.sh up`). Disable with WITH_OBSERVABILITY=0.
65	# Grafana lives on host port 3010 once the stack is up.

70	# and api services default to `http://tempo:4318` over the shared backend
71	# network when the observability stack is on. Override to point at a
72	# different collector, or set empty to disable trace export entirely.
73	# OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://tempo:4318
74	# OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=boringstack-api          # shows up as `service.name` in Tempo

76	# --- Alertmanager receivers (optional) ----------------------------------
77	# Alertmanager runs as part of observability and the bundled rules.yml
78	# fires alerts on API 5xx spikes, Postgres health, disk/memory pressure,
79	# etc. Without a receiver URL set, alerts surface in the Alertmanager UI
80	# only (http://localhost:9093 in dev). Set either or both of:
81	#
82	# Slack-format webhook. Discord also accepts Slack format — paste your
83	# Discord webhook URL with `/slack` appended (e.g.
84	# https://discord.com/api/webhooks/.../slack) to route alerts there.
85	# ALERTMANAGER_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL=https://hooks.slack.com/services/T.../B.../...
86	# ALERTMANAGER_SLACK_CHANNEL=#alerts
87	#
88	# Generic webhook receiving Alertmanager's native JSON. Use for custom
89	# bridges (n8n, your own alerter, PagerDuty's events-v2 API, etc.).
90	# ALERTMANAGER_WEBHOOK_URL=https://...

92	# See docs/alerts.md for receiver-specific setup walkthroughs.
